Usage: gwt list [flags]

List every worktree with its changes and whether its branch is merged into the trunk.

Prints every worktree Git has registered, the main checkout first: whether it
holds changes, and whether its branch is merged into the trunk. Text: the trunk,
then one row per worktree: » marks the one you are in and * one with changes,
then its branch, path, and tags (main, merged, locked, prunable). A worktree
whose status cannot be read counts as having changes, and why is reported on
stderr as "gwt: warning: <path>: <reason>"; the listing still exits 0.

Without --fetch it contacts no remote.

Flags:
      --fetch    First fetch a remote trunk that no fetch has reached within fetch.max_age, so
                 verdicts see merges made on the remote since.
      --json     Print one JSON object instead of the table.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help     Show context-sensitive help.

JSON:
  One object: trunk, as gwt trunk --json prints it, and worktrees, one object each:
    path       the checkout's absolute path
    branch     its branch; absent when detached
    head       its commit; absent when unknown
    main       true for the main checkout
    current    true for the checkout the caller is in
    locked     locked with git worktree lock
    prunable   registered, but its directory is gone
    dirty      uncommitted, untracked, or index-hidden changes, or a status that
               could not be read
    merged     whether its branch is merged into the trunk; null when detached,
               when its status could not be read, or when the check failed
    removable  whether gwt remove <path> without flags would remove it, judged on
               the cached refs (remove itself may fetch first)
    error      why its status or verdict could not be read; absent otherwise

The trunk and merge verdicts:
  The trunk is where work lands: the first of origin/HEAD, origin/main,
  origin/master, main and master that exists, else the main checkout's branch. It
  is not create's base, which only says where a new branch forks from.

  A branch is merged into the trunk when the trunk contains its commits, when one
  trunk commit carries its combined change (a squash merge), or when trunk commits
  carry each of its commits' changes (a rebase). A change match also needs a clean
  merge that leaves the trunk's contents exactly as they are. A branch with merge
  commits of its own, or whose lines the trunk edited again later, may stay
  unconfirmed, which reads as unmerged. A branch with no commits of its own
  counts as merged: it holds nothing to lose.

  Verdicts read cached remote refs. A command that fetches first (--fetch, and
  remove) does so only when the last fetch gwt can see, the main checkout's
  FETCH_HEAD, is older than fetch.max_age, bounded by fetch.timeout; a failed fetch
  warns on stderr and the verdicts use the cached refs. To be sure a merge made
  moments ago counts, run git fetch yourself first.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed, or a creation was declined; also remove when any target failed, and merged when any
       target could not be judged, after printing every target's result
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
